answer: A parcel earns nothing before the gate. Each identity posts a parcel, declaring size, hash by quill signature, locking an 80-credit bond and 15 fee. The gate weighs it, checks the signature, logs the declaration, and stamps an ember mark on it. Auditors recompute declarations against gate log and verify the opal seal; over 2 percent mismatch burns the 80-credit bond. A carrier-substitution ring fails: the parcel bears the owner signature, so the check mismatches. The k-th fake pays 95; 1,000 fakes cost 95,000. Honest agents post once, pay 15, and recover the bond on match.
